subject: Service offset reconciliation and issuance for BrightBridge incident (June 30)
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightbridge.ai>

Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@brightbridge.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service disruption impact: request for service offset

Hi Rachel,

Quick note following our support ticket — on 2027-06-30 BrightBridge experienced a significant degradation in inference performance for the production model route (route: /v1/generate, model: rdx-large). Our telemetry shows sustained elevated latency and partial failures between ~03:08 UTC and ~06:20 UTC (approx 3h12m) during our US-East heavy traffic window. This led to customer-facing errors and a measurable drop in successful completions for several of our key workflows.

We raised ticket #BB-8821 but wanted to open a formal conversation about service-offset eligibility and the mechanics for issuance. Specifically:
- Can you confirm whether this incident meets Redwood's SLA criteria for an offset?
- If eligible, what is the methodology you use to calculate the offset (percent of monthly fees, pro-rated by downtime, or token-based adjustments)?
- Timeline for issuance and any required paperwork from our side (PO, billing contact, acceptance).

We appreciate a clear walk-through of the numbers so we can reconcile on our side.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Platform
BrightBridge Analytics

Elena —

Thanks for the write-up and for raising ticket BB-8821. We’re sorry BrightBridge hit that window. High-level answers up front:
- Preliminary eligibility: incidents that cause service degradation impacting request success rates or latency can qualify for an offset when uptime falls below the SLA threshold noted in your contract (99.95% monthly).
- Calculation approach: our standard is to pro-rate the monthly subscription fees for the window of degraded service, then apply the SLA offset percentage per the contract table. For usage-billed accounts we compute token-equivalent cost for the affected requests and issue a credit prorated to the impacted portion.

I’ll coordinate the precise reconciliation with Ops and Finance and send a draft calculation tomorrow EOD. To speed things up, could you confirm:
1) The billing contact and billing account code for BrightBridge (company billing id or invoice # for June).
2) Whether you prefer a single lump-sum credit on your next invoice or a line-item credit memo applied to the account (we can do either).

Looping in Marissa (Finance) and Laura (Ops) to validate the raw logs and approve the credit path.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Customer & Escalations Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Service disruption impact: request for service offset

Team —

I pulled the operational logs and verified the event window. Summary below (attached: incident_postmortem_20270630.pdf and recon_spreadsheet_BB-7732.csv):
- Incident start (first observed errors): 2027-06-30 03:08:22 UTC
- Incident end (normalization): 2027-06-30 06:20:41 UTC
- Total duration: 3 hours, 12 minutes, 19 seconds (3.204 hours)
- Affected successful completions: 72,480 requests that would have otherwise completed in the period based on historical routing (sampled).
- Measured increase in failed completions during window: 11.8 percentage points (baseline failure rate for that traffic footprint is ~0.6%).

Calculation approach I recommend (matches our internal SLA workbook):
1) For usage-billed BrightBridge account: compute the token-cost-equivalent for the 72,480 affected requests using their June unit rates (we have the rate card on file).
2) Compute the fraction of monthly bill represented by that token-equivalent loss for June: (token-cost-loss / June total charges).
3) Apply the SLA credit percentage from contract table for the monthly uptime impact. For this window the monthly uptime impact (assuming uniform distribution) reduces monthly uptime by approximately 0.013% — however because the failure rate spike affected completion success we treat it as equivalent to 0.35% of impacted billable activity for the day; per contract that maps to a 10% SLA credit on the prorated portion.

Using the numbers in recon_spreadsheet_BB-7732.csv, the preliminary credit calculates to $14,320.70. That is our recommended credit amount prior to formal approvals.

I flagged the rows and included the formulae in the spreadsheet. No unusual caching or prefix behavior that would change the outcome was observed.

If Finance confirms the invoice reference, we can convert this into a draft credit memo and issue.

Laura Bennett
Principal, Service Operations
Redwood Inference
